record.current_timing: 2 linked phases; see Chronology phases; do not add overlapping durations
record.current_corrections: Formal Uganda–DRC ordinary-movement restriction commenced immediately in the signed May27,2026 notice and was reported current on May28. Cargo, response, humanitarian and security exceptions are explicit. The one-day minimum is a formal-policy date difference only; no expiry, physical onset or operational duration is inferred. The June15 certificate notice is unrelated to repeal. Ordinary-trader restrictions at Kasindi–Mpondwe are reported on May29 and July14; August18 documents a medical-referral permission, not general reopening. The October15 journalist visit found cargo crossing while ordinary markets and public transport remained suspended. These are dated observations, not a proved continuous May–October spell. Actual onset and reopening stay unknown; Ebola-free announcements and a June certificate notice are not endpoints.
record.rationale_coding_status: Source-attributed coding accepted after separate challenge; qualifications retained
record.rationale_phase_note: The signed Ugandan notice explicitly attributes the measure to limiting cross-border Ebola risk. The operational sources describe the same health restrictions, without proving a continuous spell or excluding every exception.
